hook.text: At a county fair, hundreds guessed an ox's weight. The average guess was off by just one pound. The experts were worse.

buildup.text: The wisdom of crowds: large groups often estimate more accurately than individuals—even experts.

discovery.text: It works when guesses are independent, diverse, and decentralized. Each person adds a unique signal.

twist.text: When people copy each other—herding—the crowd becomes a mob and accuracy collapses.

climax.text: Prediction markets work on this principle: aggregate independent bets and the price reflects collective knowledge.

punchline.text: Many independent minds beat one brilliant one.

quiz.question: What condition makes the wisdom of crowds work?
options: Guesses are independent, diverse, and decentralized
The crowd must be very large
